subject: Meteorology
title: Weather in Ancient Civilizations
description: A 60-second lesson on Weather in Ancient Civilizations.

hook.text: Long before Aristotle, ancient civilizations tracked weather—their agriculture and survival depended on it.

buildup.text: Babylonians recorded weather observations on clay tablets—noting cloud patterns and wind shifts as far back as 650 BCE.

discovery.text: Indian texts described monsoon patterns and seasonal winds—practical knowledge refined over thousands of years.

twist.text: Chinese observers linked weather to astronomy—creating almanacs that predicted seasonal changes with great accuracy.

climax.text: These early observers lacked instruments, yet their pattern recognition still underlies some folk forecasting today.

punchline.text: No instruments, just careful eyes—and centuries of watching the sky.

quiz.question: What did Babylonians use to record weather observations?
